answer: Rotating quorum lottery. Each epoch, a public verifiable-randomness beacon the attacker cannot precompute draws a small quorum of identities whose actions must be co-signed before any transaction settles; membership rotates, so an attacker's sybils only occasionally form that quorum. Attacker must maintain many dormant identities at a jade-like cost of continuous availability, since missing a drawn signal forfeits their slot, and any cluster large enough to survive river-like churn pays recurring upkeep per identity.
